category: Scripting DOM II - Application and Document members (ExtendScript)
description: The ExtendScript (JSX) Application and Document members not covered by the overview entries in 'Automation and scripting': properties, utility methods, persistence, notifiers, history, metadata, guides, layer comps, samplers, measurement, mode conversion and printing. Signatures follow the Adobe Photoshop JavaScript Scripting Reference; the equivalent UXP members are noted where they exist.

tools.name: app.activeDocument
tools.description: The front-most document; read it to operate on what the user is looking at, assign a Document to switch focus. Throws 'No document is open' when app.documents.length is 0, so guard batch scripts. Most DOM operations implicitly act on the active document and its activeLayer.
tools.usage: var doc = app.activeDocument;   app.activeDocument = app.documents[1];   app.activeDocument = app.documents.getByName("hero.psd");
tools.notes: UXP: `require('photoshop').app.activeDocument` (23.0+, settable). Switching documents in a loop is slow with large files; keep a reference to each Document object instead of re-resolving by name.

tools.name: app.foregroundColor and app.backgroundColor
tools.description: The two toolbar swatches as SolidColor objects. Assign a new SolidColor (or edit `.rgb`, `.cmyk`, `.hsb`, `.lab`, `.gray` sub-objects) before commands that use the swatches: Selection.fill(app.foregroundColor), Clouds, Neon Glow, Sketch filters, Stroke, and the Brush tool in actions.

parameters.name: SolidColor.rgb / cmyk / hsb / lab / gray
parameters.description: Colour models; setting any converts the others. `.rgb.hexValue` takes 'RRGGBB'.

parameters.name: SolidColor.model
parameters.description: ColorModel enum of the model last set.

parameters.name: SolidColor.nearestWebColor / isEqual()
parameters.description: Helpers for web palettes and comparisons.

tools.notes: Colours are converted through the document's colour profile when filled. UXP: `app.foregroundColor` (SolidColor with `.rgb`, `.hsb` etc.).

tools.name: app.preferences (Preferences object)
tools.description: Read/write access to most Edit > Preferences settings: `rulerUnits` and `typeUnits` (set these at the top of every script so UnitValue results are predictable), `interpolation`, `colorPicker`, `exportClipboard`, `maximizeCompatibility`, `useHistoryLog`/`saveLogItems`/`editLogItems`, `numberOfHistoryStates`, `imageCacheLevels`, `maxRAMuse`, `imagePreviews`, `appendExtension`, `useLowerCaseExtension`, `transparencyGridSize`, `gamutWarningOpacity`, `showToolTips`, `beepWhenDone`, `zoomWithScrollWheel` and more.
tools.usage: app.preferences.rulerUnits = Units.PIXELS;   app.preferences.typeUnits = TypeUnits.PIXELS;   var old = app.preferences.rulerUnits;

parameters.name: rulerUnits
parameters.description: Units.PIXELS | INCHES | CM | MM | POINTS | PICAS | PERCENT.

parameters.name: typeUnits
parameters.description: TypeUnits.PIXELS | POINTS | MM.

parameters.name: interpolation
parameters.description: ResampleMethod default for transforms.

parameters.name: maximizeCompatibility
parameters.description: MaximizeCompatibility.ALWAYS | NEVER | ASK.

parameters.name: useHistoryLog / saveLogItems / editLogItems
parameters.description: History log on/off, SaveLogItemsType, EditLogItemsType.

tools.notes: Changes persist beyond the script - always restore what you changed. UXP: `app.preferences` (24.0+) exposes categories such as `preferences.general`, `.cursors`, `.unitsAndRulers`, `.notifications`.

tools.name: app.displayDialogs (DialogModes)
tools.description: Controls whether commands run from the script show their dialogs: DialogModes.ALL shows every dialog, DialogModes.ERROR shows only error dialogs, DialogModes.NO suppresses everything (missing parameters take defaults and errors throw). Set NO for unattended batch scripts; executeAction takes the same enum as its third argument per call.
tools.notes: DialogModes.NO does not suppress ScriptUI alerts or the 'trusted source' script warning. The property is reset to ALL when the script ends. UXP: `app.displayDialogs` with constants.DialogModes.

tools.name: app.version, app.build, app.path, app.locale and app.systemInformation
tools.description: Read-only environment facts: `version` ('26.0.0'), `build`, `path` (Folder of Photoshop.exe, used to find Presets), `name`, `locale` ('en_US'), `freeMemory`, `scriptingVersion` and `scriptingBuildDate`, `systemInformation` (the same text as Help > System Info), `windowsFileTypes` / `macintoshFileTypes` (arrays of openable extensions/types). Use them to branch on version and to build absolute paths.
tools.usage: app.version   app.build   app.path   app.locale   app.systemInformation   app.freeMemory   app.windowsFileTypes
tools.notes: `app.path` is the application folder; user presets live under Folder.userData ('%AppData%/Adobe/Adobe Photoshop <ver>/Presets'). UXP: `require('uxp').host.version` and `host.name`.

tools.name: app.fonts (TextFonts collection)
tools.description: The fonts Photoshop can use, as TextFont objects with `name` (menu name), `postScriptName` (the value TextItem.font expects), `family` and `style`. Iterate it to map a display name to a PostScript name, to check that a required font is installed before running a template, or to build a font picker in ScriptUI.
tools.notes: Enumerating thousands of fonts is slow (seconds); cache the result. Adobe Fonts activated through Creative Cloud appear here once synced. UXP: `app.fonts`.

tools.name: app.refresh(), app.purge(), app.beep(), app.togglePalettes(), app.bringToFront()
tools.description: Small utilities: `refresh()` redraws the screen (call inside long loops so progress is visible), `purge(PurgeTarget.ALLCACHES | CLIPBOARDCACHE | HISTORYCACHES | UNDOCACHES)` frees memory like Edit > Purge, `beep()` signals completion, `togglePalettes()` hides/shows panels like the Tab key, and `bringToFront()` raises the Photoshop window (useful after COM launches).

parameters.name: PurgeTarget
parameters.description: ALLCACHES, CLIPBOARDCACHE, HISTORYCACHES, UNDOCACHES.

tools.notes: Purging history inside a script cannot be undone by the user afterwards. UXP: `app.bringToFront()`; use `core.redrawDocument()` to force a redraw.

tools.name: app.batch() and BatchOptions
tools.description: Runs a recorded action over an array of files exactly like File > Automate > Batch, with a BatchOptions object controlling destination (NOSAVE, SAVEANDCLOSE, FOLDER), file naming tokens, suppression of Open/Color Profile dialogs, override of Open/Save As commands and error handling. Use it instead of hand-rolled loops when the processing is already an action.

parameters.name: inputFiles
parameters.description: Array of File objects.

parameters.name: action / from
parameters.description: Action name and the action set name.

parameters.name: options.destination
parameters.description: BatchDestinationType.NOSAVE | SAVEANDCLOSE | FOLDER (with `destinationFolder`).

parameters.name: options.fileNaming
parameters.description: Array of FileNamingType tokens, e.g. [DOCUMENTNAMEMIXED, EXTENSIONLOWER].

parameters.name: options.overrideOpen / overrideSave / suppressOpen / suppressProfile / errorFile
parameters.description: Match the Batch dialog checkboxes; errorFile logs errors instead of stopping.

tools.notes: The action set and action must exist in the Actions panel. Returns the name of the last processed file; check `errorFile` afterwards.

tools.name: app.load(), app.openDialog() and app.system()
tools.description: `load(file)` opens a support document (e.g. a displacement map or pattern source) without making it the active document for the user; `openDialog()` shows the Open dialog and returns the chosen Files without opening them; `system(command)` executes an OS shell command (cmd on Windows, sh on macOS) synchronously and returns its exit status - handy for launching helper tools or moving files.
tools.usage: app.load(file);   var files = app.openDialog();   var rc = app.system("cmd /c copy \"C:\\out\\a.jpg\" \"D:\\backup\\\"");
tools.notes: For a single file/folder picker use `File.openDialog()`, `File.saveDialog()` and `Folder.selectDialog()` from the ExtendScript file API. `app.system` blocks Photoshop until the command finishes.

tools.name: app.notifiers (Notifier) and app.notifiersEnabled
tools.description: Programmatic access to the Script Events Manager: `app.notifiers.add(event, eventFile, extension)` binds a script file to an event ID such as 'Opn ' (open document), 'Nw  ' (new document), 'Sav ' (save), 'Prnt' (print), 'Cls ' (close) or a stringID like 'exportDocument'; `notifiersEnabled` toggles all of them; `notifiers.removeAll()` clears. Use it to auto-run watermarking, logging or validation on every open/save without user action.
tools.usage: app.notifiers.add(event, eventFile [, extension]);   app.notifiersEnabled = true;   app.notifiers.removeAll();

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: Four-character event ID ('Opn ', 'Sav ', 'Cls ', 'Prnt', 'Nw  ', 'Mk  ') or a stringID; the Script Events Manager dialog lists them.

parameters.name: eventFile
parameters.description: File of the .jsx to run.

parameters.name: extension
parameters.description: Optional class ID filter, e.g. 'Dcmn' for document events.

tools.notes: The handler script gets the event ID and ActionDescriptor as `arguments[0]` and `arguments[1]`. Events fire for scripted operations too, so guard against recursion.

tools.name: app.playbackDisplayDialogs and app.playbackParameters
tools.description: Support recording scripts into actions with parameters: when a script is inserted in an action (File > Scripts from the Actions panel), `playbackParameters` holds an ActionDescriptor the script can populate so the action stores and replays the user's choices, and `playbackDisplayDialogs` mirrors the action's dialog-toggle for that step. This is how Image Processor and Fit Image remember settings inside actions.
tools.usage: var params = app.playbackParameters;   app.playbackParameters = desc;   if (app.playbackDisplayDialogs == DialogModes.ALL) { /* show UI */ }
tools.notes: Only meaningful when the script is run from an action step; when run directly `playbackDisplayDialogs` is ALL and the descriptor is empty.

tools.name: app.putCustomOptions(), getCustomOptions() and eraseCustomOptions()
tools.description: Persist an ActionDescriptor of settings under a string key in Photoshop's preferences (optionally 'persistent' across sessions) so a script or ScriptUI dialog can remember its last values - the standard way Adobe's own scripts store options without writing files.
tools.usage: app.putCustomOptions(key, descriptor, persistent);   var d = app.getCustomOptions(key);   app.eraseCustomOptions(key);

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Unique string, e.g. a reverse-DNS name 'com.example.exporter'.

parameters.name: descriptor
parameters.description: ActionDescriptor containing the values to store.

parameters.name: persistent
parameters.description: true keeps the data after Photoshop quits.

tools.notes: `getCustomOptions` throws if the key does not exist - wrap it in try/catch. Data is lost when preferences are reset. UXP plugins use `localStorage` or `uxp.storage` data folder instead.

tools.name: typeIDToStringID() and typeIDToCharID()
tools.description: The reverse of stringIDToTypeID/charIDToTypeID: convert a numeric type ID back into its readable string or four-character ID. Used when dumping ActionDescriptors returned by executeActionGet or events received by notifiers, so keys and enum values can be logged or matched by name.
tools.notes: Some IDs have only a charID or only a stringID; the other conversion returns an empty string. UXP batchPlay returns descriptors already in string form (`_obj`, `_enum`).

tools.name: app.runMenuItem()
tools.description: Executes any menu command by its command ID, covering the handful of menu items that neither the DOM nor a recorded Action Manager event reaches (e.g. Fit on Screen, Actual Pixels, Toggle rulers). IDs are obtained from `charIDToTypeID` for the classic four-character command IDs or from the menu command numbers listed by Adobe's 'menu commands' resource.

parameters.name: commandID
parameters.description: Integer menu command ID (e.g. charIDToTypeID('FtOn') = Fit on Screen, 'ActP' = 100 %, 'Undo' = Undo, 'RlrT' = Toggle rulers).

tools.example:
app.runMenuItem(charIDToTypeID("FtOn"));   // View > Fit on Screen
app.runMenuItem(charIDToTypeID("ActP"));   // View > 100%
tools.notes: Not documented in the official reference but stable since CS3. UXP: `core.performMenuCommand({ commandID })` with numeric IDs and `core.getMenuCommandState()`.

tools.name: Document.activeLayer and layer targeting
tools.description: The currently selected layer (ArtLayer or LayerSet); assign any layer object to select it, which most ArtLayer methods and filters require. Only one layer is 'active' in the DOM even when several are selected in the panel; use Action Manager 'selectAllLayers'/'select' descriptors for multi-selection. `doc.layers`, `doc.artLayers` and `doc.layerSets` are indexed top-to-bottom and searchable with getByName().
tools.usage: doc.activeLayer = doc.artLayers.getByName("hero");   doc.activeLayer = doc.layerSets[0].artLayers[2];   var lyr = doc.activeLayer;
tools.notes: `getByName` searches only the given collection (not nested groups) and returns the first match. Activating a layer inside a collapsed group expands it in the panel. UXP: `doc.activeLayers` (array, multi-select aware).

tools.name: Document.historyStates, activeHistoryState and HistoryState
tools.description: The History panel as a collection of HistoryState objects (`name`, `snapshot` boolean); set `activeHistoryState` to revert to a state and `activeHistoryBrushSource` to set the History Brush source. Snapshots created via Action Manager ('make' with class 'snapshotClass') appear here with `snapshot = true`. Useful for undoing a whole scripted operation in one step.
tools.notes: History is limited by Preferences > Performance > History States; long scripts exhaust it. Prefer `doc.suspendHistory()` to collapse a script into one undo step. UXP: `doc.historyStates`, `doc.activeHistoryState`.

tools.name: Document.suspendHistory()
tools.description: Runs a string of JavaScript while recording only a single, named history state, so the user can undo the whole script with one Ctrl+Z and the History panel is not flooded. The code runs in the global scope via eval, so pass a function name defined earlier.

parameters.name: historyStateName
parameters.description: Label shown in the History panel.

parameters.name: javaScriptCode
parameters.description: String evaluated while history is suspended, e.g. 'main()'.

tools.notes: Errors inside the suspended block still leave a single state. UXP: `await doc.suspendHistory(async () => {...}, "name")` (23.0+) or `executeAsModal` with `historyStateInfo`.

tools.name: Document.info (DocumentInfo metadata)
tools.description: Read/write access to the File Info (IPTC/XMP) fields: `title`, `author`, `authorPosition`, `caption`, `captionWriter`, `headline`, `instructions`, `keywords` (array), `copyrightNotice`, `copyrighted` (CopyrightedType), `owner`/`ownerUrl`, `credit`, `source`, `category`, `supplementalCategories`, `city`, `provinceState`, `country`, `jobName`, `creationDate`, `transmissionReference`, `urgency`, and read-only `exif` (array of [tag, value] pairs). Populate it before export to stamp copyright and keywords into JPEG/TIFF/PSD files.
tools.usage: doc.info.copyrightNotice = "(c) 2026 Studio";   doc.info.keywords = ["product", "hero"];   var exif = doc.info.exif;
tools.notes: EXIF is read-only here; edit via XMP (`doc.xmpMetadata`). Export As strips most metadata unless 'Copyright and Contact Info' is chosen.

tools.name: Document.xmpMetadata and the AdobeXMPScript library
tools.description: `doc.xmpMetadata.rawData` is the document's complete XMP packet as an XML string (read/write). For structured access load the XMP scripting library with `new ExternalObject("lib:AdobeXMPScript")`, then use XMPMeta/XMPConst to get, set and enumerate properties in any namespace (Dublin Core, photoshop, xmpRights, camera raw settings, custom schemas).
tools.usage: var xml = doc.xmpMetadata.rawData;   doc.xmpMetadata.rawData = xml;   if (ExternalObject.AdobeXMPScript == undefined) ExternalObject.AdobeXMPScript = new ExternalObject("lib:AdobeXMPScript");
tools.notes: Custom namespaces need `XMPMeta.registerNamespace(uri, prefix)`. XMP written this way is saved with PSD/TIFF/JPEG/PNG. UXP has no XMP library yet; use batchPlay 'get' on 'XMPMetadataAsUTF8' or parse the string.

tools.name: Document.guides (Guides and Guide)
tools.description: Collection of the document's guides: `guides.add(direction, coordinate)` creates one, each Guide has `direction` (Direction.HORIZONTAL/VERTICAL) and `coordinate` (UnitValue in ruler units) and `remove()`. Use it to lay out grids, safe areas and columns programmatically, or to read guide positions to drive slicing/cropping.
tools.notes: Available since CC 2014. Artboard guides and per-guide colours (2020+) are only reachable via Action Manager. UXP: `doc.guides` (23.0+).

tools.name: Document.layerComps (LayerComps and LayerComp)
tools.description: Layer comps as objects: `layerComps.add(name, comment, appearance, position, visibility, childLayerCompState)` creates a comp capturing the chosen attributes; each LayerComp has `apply()` to switch to it, `recapture()` to update it from the current state, `resetFromComp()`, `remove()`, and `selected`. Scripts iterate comps to export each state (as Layer Comps to Files does).
tools.usage: doc.layerComps.add(name, comment, appearance, position, visibility [, childLayerCompState]);   doc.layerComps[i].apply();   doc.layerComps.getByName("Dark").recapture();

parameters.name: appearance / position / visibility
parameters.description: Booleans: capture layer styles, positions, visibility.

parameters.name: childLayerCompState
parameters.description: Capture nested Smart Object comp selections (CC 2014+).

tools.notes: The 'Last Document State' pseudo-comp is not in the collection. UXP: `doc.layerComps` (24.0+).

tools.name: Document.colorSamplers (ColorSamplers and ColorSampler)
tools.description: The Color Sampler tool's points as objects: `colorSamplers.add([x, y])` places one (up to 10), each ColorSampler exposes `position` and `color` (a SolidColor read from the composite at that point), plus `move([x, y])` and `remove()`. A precise way to read pixel colours in scripts without touching the clipboard.
tools.usage: var s = doc.colorSamplers.add([UnitValue(100,"px"), UnitValue(200,"px")]);   s.color.rgb.red   s.move([x, y]);   doc.colorSamplers.removeAll();
tools.notes: Readings are taken from the visible composite (all layers) in the document colour mode. The sample size follows the Eyedropper's Sample Size option. UXP: `doc.colorSamplers` (24.0+) and `doc.sampleColor(position)`.

tools.name: Document.countItems and autoCount()
tools.description: Objects for the Count tool: `countItems.add([x, y])` places a count marker, each CountItem has `position` and `remove()`, and `doc.autoCount(channel, threshold)` runs Image > Analysis > Count (auto count of objects in a channel above a threshold). Used for cell/particle counting in scientific images together with the Measurement Log.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Channel object to analyse (typically a thresholded alpha).

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.description: 0-255 level separating objects from background.

tools.notes: Auto count needs a binary (thresholded) channel; noise inflates the count - run Median/Despeckle first. Count groups (colours) are Action Manager only.

tools.name: Document.measurementScale and recordMeasurements()
tools.description: `measurementScale` (pixelLength, logicalLength, logicalUnits) defines how many pixels equal one real-world unit (Image > Analysis > Set Measurement Scale) so the Ruler tool, Count and Record Measurements report in microns or millimetres; `recordMeasurements(source, dataPoints)` appends a row to the Measurement Log for the selection, count items or ruler with the chosen data points (area, perimeter, circularity, height, width, grey values...).

parameters.name: MeasurementSource
parameters.description: MEASURESELECTION, MEASURECOUNTTOOL, MEASURERULERTOOL.

parameters.name: dataPoints
parameters.description: Array of data point names, e.g. Area, Perimeter, Circularity, Height, Width, GrayValueMean, IntegratedDensity, Histogram, Label, Date, Source, Scale, ScaleUnits.

tools.notes: Measurement features are available in all current Photoshop editions (formerly Extended only). The log is exported via the panel; `app.measurementLog.exportMeasurements(file, range, dataPoints)` scripts it.

tools.name: Document properties: bitsPerChannel, mode, colorProfileName, resolution, width/height, name/fullName/path, saved, managed
tools.description: The read-mostly facts about a document: `bitsPerChannel` (BitsPerChannelType, settable to convert 8/16/32), `mode` (DocumentMode), `colorProfileName` (settable = Assign Profile) and `colorProfileType`, `resolution` (ppi), `width`/`height` (UnitValue in ruler units), `name`, `fullName` (File) and `path` (Folder; both throw for unsaved documents), `saved` (no unsaved changes), `managed` (Version Cue legacy), `histogram` (array of 256 counts for the composite), `pixelAspectRatio`, `quickMaskMode`, `backgroundLayer`, `componentChannels`.
tools.usage: doc.bitsPerChannel = BitsPerChannelType.EIGHT;   doc.mode   doc.colorProfileName = "sRGB IEC61966-2.1";   doc.width.as("px")   doc.fullName.fsName   doc.saved
tools.notes: `doc.fullName` throws 'The document has not been saved' for new documents - check with try/catch. UXP exposes the same as plain properties (`doc.path` is a string, `doc.cloudDocument` flags cloud files).

tools.name: Document.duplicate()
tools.description: Creates a copy of the document (Image > Duplicate) and returns the new Document, optionally flattening it (`mergeLayersOnly = true` duplicates merged layers only). The standard first step for destructive exports so the original stays untouched and open.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the new document (default '<name> copy').

parameters.name: mergeLayersOnly
parameters.description: true = duplicate as a flattened composite.

tools.notes: The duplicate becomes the active document. UXP: `await doc.duplicate(name, mergeLayersOnly)`.

tools.name: Document.flatten() and mergeVisibleLayers()
tools.description: `flatten()` merges every layer into a single Background layer, discarding hidden layers and transparency (filled with the background colour) - required before saving to formats without layers; `mergeVisibleLayers()` merges only the visible layers into the active one and keeps hidden layers and transparency. Both are destructive; duplicate first if the source must survive.
tools.notes: Flatten applies layer masks and rasterises type and Smart Objects. `rasterizeAllLayers()` rasterises without merging. UXP: `await doc.flatten()`, `await doc.mergeVisibleLayers()`.

tools.name: Document.changeMode()
tools.description: Converts the colour mode (Image > Mode): ChangeMode.RGB, CMYK, LAB, GRAYSCALE, BITMAP (with BitmapConversionOptions), INDEXEDCOLOR (with IndexedConversionOptions: palette, colors, dither, transparency), MULTICHANNEL. Conversions to Bitmap and Indexed require 8-bit grayscale/RGB respectively; Photoshop may prompt to flatten unless dialogs are off.

parameters.name: destinationMode
parameters.description: ChangeMode enum.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: BitmapConversionOptions {method, resolution, angle, frequency, shape, patternName} or IndexedConversionOptions {palette, colors, forced, dither, ditherAmount, matte, preserveExactColors, transparency}.

tools.notes: RGB->CMYK uses the Color Settings CMYK profile; use `convertProfile()` for an explicit press profile. UXP: `await doc.changeMode(mode, options)`.

tools.name: Document.paste()
tools.description: Pastes the clipboard contents as a new layer, optionally into the current selection (`paste(true)` = Edit > Paste Special > Paste Into, which creates a layer mask from the selection). Combined with `selection.copy()`/`copy(true)` (merged) it moves pixels between documents in scripts.

parameters.name: intoSelection
parameters.description: true pastes inside the active selection and masks the result.

tools.notes: Pasted layers are centred in the visible area; use `layer.translate()` to position, or Action Manager 'paste' with 'inPlace'. Clipboard transfers are slow for huge selections - `ArtLayer.duplicate(otherDoc)` avoids the clipboard entirely.

tools.name: Document.splitChannels()
tools.description: Splits a flattened document into one grayscale document per channel (Channels panel menu > Split Channels) and returns the array of new documents, closing the original. Used to write individual channels to files or to feed channel data into other tools.
tools.notes: The document must be flattened (a single layer). Merge Channels (the reverse) is Action Manager only ('mergeChannels').

tools.name: Document.rasterizeAllLayers() and revealAll()
tools.description: `rasterizeAllLayers()` converts every type, shape, fill and Smart Object layer to pixels without merging (Layer > Rasterize > All Layers) - handy before filters that need pixel layers everywhere; `revealAll()` enlarges the canvas so that every layer's pixels fit inside it (Image > Reveal All), the counterpart of Trim.
tools.notes: Both are destructive for vector/smart content; UXP has `doc.rasterizeAllLayers()` and `doc.revealAll()` as async methods.

tools.name: Document.print(), printOneCopy() and printSettings
tools.description: Send the document to a printer from a script: `printOneCopy()` prints with the last-used settings, `print(sourceSpace, printSpace, intent, blackPointCompensation)` prints with explicit colour management, and `printSettings` (DocumentPrintSettings) exposes the Print dialog fields - printer name, copies, colour handling, printer profile, rendering intent, black point compensation, position (top/left/centre), scale, hard proofing, background colour, border, bleed and registration marks.
tools.usage: doc.printOneCopy();   doc.print(SourceSpaceType.DOCUMENT, "Epson SC-P900 Premium Luster", Intent.RELATIVECOLORIMETRIC, true);   doc.printSettings.copies = 2;

parameters.name: printSettings.activePrinter / printerList
parameters.description: Choose among installed printers.

parameters.name: printSettings.colorHandling
parameters.description: PrintColorHandling.PRINTERMANAGED | PHOTOSHOPMANAGED | SEPARATIONS.

parameters.name: printSettings.printSpace / renderingIntent / blackPointCompensation
parameters.description: Output profile and mapping when Photoshop manages colours.

parameters.name: printSettings.centerImage / posX / posY / scale / printSelected
parameters.description: Layout options.

tools.notes: Printer driver dialogs cannot be suppressed by DialogModes. Not available in UXP; use batchPlay 'print'.

tools.name: Document.save() and Document.saved
tools.description: `save()` writes the document back to its current file in its current format (File > Save) and throws for never-saved documents, where `saveAs()` is required; `saved` reports whether there are unsaved changes. Use them in watch-folder and event-driven scripts to persist edits without changing file names.
tools.notes: Saving a JPEG-opened document with `save()` re-compresses it (quality dialog suppressed by DialogModes.NO uses the last settings). UXP: `await doc.save()`.

tools.name: Document.backgroundLayer
tools.description: Returns the locked Background layer (ArtLayer with `isBackgroundLayer = true`) or throws if the document has none. Set `isBackgroundLayer = false` on it to unlock (Layer from Background), or `true` on the bottom layer to create one. Many export formats and Automate scripts expect a Background layer.
tools.notes: Only a bottom-most, fully opaque pixel layer can become the Background. UXP: `doc.backgroundLayer` returns null when absent.

tools.name: Document.pixelAspectRatio and quickMaskMode
tools.description: `pixelAspectRatio` (0.05-10) sets the View > Pixel Aspect Ratio used for non-square video pixels (e.g. 1.21 for D1/DV PAL) so the preview is corrected while the pixel data is not; `quickMaskMode` toggles Quick Mask editing, turning the current selection into a paintable channel and back.
tools.notes: Filters applied in Quick Mask affect the mask, not the layer. UXP: `doc.quickMaskMode` (23.0+), `doc.pixelAspectRatio`.

tools.name: Documents.add() options (new document parameters)
tools.description: The full signature of `app.documents.add(width, height, resolution, name, mode, initialFill, pixelAspectRatio, bitsPerChannel, colorProfileName)`: mode is NewDocumentMode (GRAYSCALE, RGB, CMYK, LAB, BITMAP), initialFill is DocumentFill (WHITE, BACKGROUNDCOLOR, TRANSPARENT), bitsPerChannel is BitsPerChannelType, and colorProfileName is an installed profile name. Width/height accept UnitValue or numbers in the current ruler unit.
tools.usage: app.documents.add([width] [, height] [, resolution] [, name] [, mode] [, initialFill] [, pixelAspectRatio] [, bitsPerChannel] [, colorProfileName])
tools.example:
app.preferences.rulerUnits = Units.PIXELS;
var doc = app.documents.add(1920, 1080, 72, "banner", NewDocumentMode.RGB, DocumentFill.TRANSPARENT, 1.0, BitsPerChannelType.SIXTEEN, "Adobe RGB (1998)");
tools.notes: Artboard documents cannot be created here; use Action Manager 'make' with 'artboard'. UXP: `app.createDocument({width, height, resolution, mode, fill, name, colorProfile, depth})` or `{preset: "..."}`.
